strategy.summary: Reproduce the wrong-sign infinity negation in sympy's EllipticCurvePoint.__neg__ by running the project's own test_elliptic_curve on the buggy checkout (22779eb67cb2), where -O yields y=-1 instead of y=1, then on the fixed revision where the early z==0 branch returns the canonical point at infinity. The transition is the assertion on (-O).x, .y, .z versus O's coordinates in the added test lines.
strategy.reproducing_test: sympy/ntheory/tests/test_elliptic_curve.py::test_elliptic_curve, extended by the added lines: O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(e3); assert (-O).x == O.x and (-O).y == O.y and (-O).z == O.z
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 22779eb67cb2 the test fails with AssertionError at the new assertion because (-O).y is -1 while O.y is 1. On the fixed revision (with the z==0 early return in __neg__) the same test function passes, including all pre-existing assertions such as the discriminant and torsion point checks.
strategy.numerical_probe: E = EllipticCurve(0, 0); O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E); neg_O = -O; print((neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z)) expected to show (0, -1, 0) on buggy and (0, 1, 0) on fixed
risks: The added test lines reference e3, which is not defined in the diff context shown; the test passes only if e3 is an EllipticCurve defined earlier in test_elliptic_curve. If it is not, the test fails with NameError on both revisions and does not discriminate the bug.
The sympy dependency is undocumented and unconstrained; installing sympy from PyPI would test a different release, so the strategy runs from the cloned checkout at the buggy commit instead.

The buggy behaviour is pure integer arithmetic with no platform, compiler, BLAS, or threading dependence, so it should transition on any Linux or macOS x86_64 or arm64 host; no sanitizer or special architecture is needed.
Python version is not stated by the evidence; any Python version supported by the buggy checkout works, and the choice of interpreter is unverified.

The reproducer in the issue uses EllipticCurve(0, 0) while the regression test uses e3; if e3 differs in a way that changes the negation formula, behaviour could differ, though the z==0 branch does not depend on the curve coefficients.
The pytest node id assumes the test file path is unchanged at the buggy commit; the fix commit's test diff targets the same file, so this should hold.

oracle.reference_source: Canonical infinity representation (0, 1, 0) stated in the issue and PR description
oracle.why: Coordinates are integers in projective form, so an exact tuple comparison is the correct oracle.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The new assertion compares (-O).y, which is -1 on the buggy revision, against O.y which is 1, so the equality fails and pytest reports AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the early return self.point_at_infinity(self._curve) when self.z == 0, (-O) has coordinates (0, 1, 0) identical to O, so the assertion holds and the test passes.
